tasks.short: Plan and implement network security measures

steps.what: Read current network security measures
Draft measures that protect software and hardware

loop.input: measure rows and the plan template
loop.output: draft that cites measure ids only
loop.check: Every cited measure id is on the current list
loop.stop: One pass, then drop any sentence with no measure id
loop.why_not_simpler: Why a control should change is not a fixed lookup

steps.what: Sign the security measures to implement
Coordinate the signed measures with the architect
File the signed security measures
Implement the signed security measures by hand

tasks.design: A {BI} view lists current measures with an owner and a system id. A bounded note in {DOCS} drafts the plan from those rows only. The systems administrator signs one version, files it, and still implements it by hand. No change runs unattended.
tasks.previous_blocker: Measure text lived in old documents and meeting notes, so a draft could not show which control it relied on.
tasks.enabler_now: Consoles can export a measure id, a system id and an owner, so each drafted row can be checked against a field.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a risky opening stays is a trade-off with the business, not a threshold.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator decides which security measures to implement and refuses one that has no owner.

ambition.what: Review security measures every month, not only after an incident

tasks.altitude: Less time rewriting the plan, same right to refuse a live change. The administrator can block a measure whose fields do not match the export.

reach.task: Check the signed measure list before a design change
reach.learn: Which security measures are signed and which rows are still blank

evidence.claim: In a mid-size firm this task is a plan plus a review. The hard part is which measure is worth the operational risk, not the formatting.
Digest [S16] and [S18] say Dutch cyber law has been in force since 15 August 2026 and, for firms in scope, the duty of care includes patching and supply-chain measures. Sector and size decide scope.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so an unattended change to live security controls is out of scope.

assumptions: Focal role is the systems administrator. The task ends when the signed measures are filed and the ones they choose are implemented. A later audit is out of scope.
Input contract: measure id, system id, owner, control type, last review date. Producer is the console export. If a row has no measure id the administrator types it and marks the row manual.

Use the document store's own template and approval flow before custom code. The meeting-heavy prior overstates this task: gathering is the console and the plan, and only the signature is a short review.
unknowns: Whether this firm is in scope of the Dutch cyber duty of care.
Who may sign a measure when the administrator is absent.
Which controls have no job interface and must stay manual.
research_questions: What share of security measures has no owner?
How often does a signed measure differ from what is live?

already_counted.description: Administrator edits the measure draft before signing
Signature time on which measures to implement
Hands-on implementation stays with the administrator

incremental.description: Update the measure template when a new control type appears
Architect time on comments beyond the first read

approvals.approved_version: security measure version signed in this review
the same signed security measure version
the same signed security measure version

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes most measures are free text, so the draft rarely matches and implementation stays fully manual. The high case assumes clean rows, while every live change still takes administrator time. Unattended changes are not counted as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Submit a request for disaster recovery
Sign the policy for data backups
Run the backups the policy names
Choose disaster recovery operations to run
Perform the signed recovery operations
Review backups that failed the check

tasks.design: A signed backup policy in {DOCS} names the jobs. Those jobs run on the {OPS_SYSTEM}. A failed job stays on a {BI} list. Disaster recovery operations run only after the administrator signs that event, and never unattended.
tasks.previous_blocker: Backup success was checked by eye and recovery steps lived in mail, so a job could not know which policy version was current.
tasks.enabler_now: Backup tools already run on a schedule. The missing piece is a signed policy version and a job id.
tasks.still_hard: A restore of the wrong system is costly, and some stores still have no job interface.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator signs the policy and chooses which disaster recovery operations to perform.

ambition.what: Night operators can see which backups failed without waiting for a morning visit

tasks.altitude: Scheduled backups leave the week. Failed jobs and recovery operations stay with the administrator, who can stop a job that looks wrong.

reach.task: Read the filed backup result before a recovery test
reach.learn: Which policy version is current and which failed backups are still open

evidence.claim: Scheduled backup jobs are already normal. The remaining human work is the policy, the restore and the failed job.
Digest [S16] and [S18] say firms in scope of the Dutch cyber duty of care have continuity obligations, including measures that keep operations going. Whether this firm is in scope is a separate fact.
Digest [S22] says security logging must stay necessary and proportionate. A backup log should record the job result and the owner, not file contents.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so an unattended restore is out of scope.

assumptions: Focal role is the systems administrator. The task covers backups and disaster recovery operations, not desktop file tidying.

Input contract: policy version, system id, job id, request type, owner. Producer of the policy fields is the administrator; the requester supplies system id and request type. A request with no system id is rejected by rule.
The meeting-heavy prior does not fit. Time today sits on the console and the job list. Native backup schedules are configured before custom code. Job logs are not used to watch staff.
Stores with no job interface stay manual. That is why the saved range sits below the case where every job is scheduled.
unknowns: Which stores still have no job interface.
Whether a restore of a personal folder needs a privacy review.
Who may sign a recovery when the administrator is away.
research_questions: What share of backups failed last month?
How many disaster recovery operations were performed last quarter?

already_counted.description: Policy signature stays with the administrator
Choice of recovery operations stays with the administrator
Failed backups review stays with the administrator

incremental.description: Revise backup policy fields when a new store type is added
Requesters resubmit a recovery that named the wrong system

approvals.approved_version: backups policy version for this period
the same signed backups policy version
disaster recovery operations signed for this event

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes many stores have no job interface, so backups stay manual and only the policy form is new. The high case assumes scheduled backups run, while every recovery and every failed job still takes administrator time. No unattended restore is counted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Resolve network problems and replace parts

steps.what: Report a hardware or software problem
Diagnose the network and system problem
Draft a troubleshoot note for this problem

loop.output: a note that cites one runbook id
loop.check: The note cites a runbook id for that symptom code
loop.stop: If no entry matches, return an empty note and stop
loop.why_not_simpler: Matching a new symptom phrase to a runbook needs reading, not a fixed table

steps.what: Decide how to resolve the problem
Resolve the signed software or system problem
Replace defective components when necessary
Confirm the hardware problem is resolved

tasks.design: A {BI} view opens on the failing system from the {OPS_SYSTEM}. A bounded note drafts a troubleshoot note from the runbook, tied to a symptom code. The administrator decides the fix, resolves it, and replaces defective components when necessary. The user confirms. Uncoded faults stay manual.
tasks.previous_blocker: Fault notes were free text in mail, so a repeated hardware problem did not line up with a runbook entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Monitoring can emit a system id and a symptom code that a runbook can key on.
tasks.still_hard: Novel faults and a swap of the wrong component still depend on the administrator.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator decides how to resolve the problem and when a defective component must be replaced.
tasks.altitude: Known faults take less gathering. The administrator keeps the right to resolve or refuse a live change.

reach.task: Confirm the system problem is gone
reach.learn: Which symptom codes already have a signed fix and which must wait

evidence.claim: Most hardware and software faults in a mid-size firm are diagnosed from monitors and then changed by hand. Only repeated, coded cases suit a runbook.
Digest [S7] and [S8] describe a managed detection service that speeds investigation for mid-size firms, while a person still decides what to do.
Digest [S13] reports an observational study of live security operations with shorter resolve times after a generative assistant versus matched peers. It was not a randomised trial.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so an unattended change while resolving a live fault is out of scope.

assumptions: Focal role is the systems administrator. The task runs from a reported problem to a confirmed resolve, a replaced component, or a stopped attempt.
Input contract: system id, symptom code, start time, site, component id. Producer is the monitoring export, or the user when no code exists. Faults without a symptom code skip the draft.
The meeting-heavy prior does not fit. Time is on the monitor, the runbook and the rack. User confirmation is a short check. Native alerting is configured before custom code.
unknowns: Whether the administrator may change production during the day.
Which devices expose a job interface versus a console only.
Who holds spare components at a small site.
research_questions: What share of problems repeat a symptom code already in the runbook?
How often is the first resolve rolled back?

already_counted.description: Administrator reviews a weak troubleshoot note before deciding
Hands-on resolve time remains with the administrator
Component replacement remains with the administrator

incremental.description: Add new symptom codes to the runbook after repeated problems

approvals.approved_version: resolve decision signed for this problem id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes most problems have no symptom code, so the note rarely fires and diagnosis stays manual. The high case assumes coded faults draft cleanly, while every resolve and every component swap stays manual. No unattended change is counted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Review computer networks and configurations
Draft systems software and applications changes

loop.output: a change note that cites configuration ids
loop.check: Every cited configuration id is on the drift list
loop.stop: Stop after one draft and drop any row with no configuration id
loop.why_not_simpler: Whether an intentional drift should stay is not a fixed table

steps.what: Sign configurations for hardware and software
Maintain networks using signed configurations
Administer environments the standard missed

tasks.design: A {BI} view shows configuration drift for computer networks against a signed standard in {DOCS}. A bounded note drafts a change only from rows with a configuration id. Standard configurations apply on the {OPS_SYSTEM} after that signature. Environments the standard misses stay on a manual list.
tasks.previous_blocker: Configurations were edited on each console and copied into documents later, so nobody could tell which version was signed.
tasks.enabler_now: Devices can export a configuration id and a drift flag that a standard can key on.
tasks.still_hard: A live change on a network that has no job interface, and a drift that is intentional, still need the administrator.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator signs the configurations and stops a change that the standard should not cover.

ambition.what: Check configuration drift every week instead of at the quarterly review

tasks.altitude: Less time collecting screenshots of drift. The administrator can refuse a configuration that has no signed version.

reach.task: Read which configurations the administrator has signed
reach.learn: Which networks match the standard and which environments are excepted

evidence.claim: Day-to-day administration of networks is console work on configurations. The quarterly workshop in the time prior is the exception, not the weekly job.
Digest [S16] and [S18] say that for firms in scope, the Dutch cyber duty of care includes patching. Scope depends on sector and size, and this task does not decide scope.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so an unattended change to live configurations is out of scope.

assumptions: Focal role is the systems administrator. The task is maintaining networks, hardware, systems software, applications software and configurations. A redesign of the network is a later task.
Input contract: configuration id, system id, drift flag, owner, standard version. Producer is the console export. Rows with no configuration id stay on the manual list.
Native configuration tools are tested before custom code. The meeting-heavy prior overstates this task: the time is on the console. Devices with no job interface never take the machine step.
unknowns: Which devices have no job interface.
Who may sign a configuration when the administrator is absent.
Whether this firm is in scope of the cyber duty of care.
research_questions: What share of configurations has no owner?
How often is a drift flag intentional?

already_counted.description: Administrator edits a weak configurations draft
Exception environments stay with the administrator

incremental.description: Extend the standard when a new device type is added

approvals.approved_version: configurations version signed in this review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes most devices have no job interface, so the apply step rarely runs and the administrator still edits by hand. The high case assumes standard configurations apply after a signature, while every exception still takes administrator time. No unattended change is counted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The administrator stops retyping security notes and backup checks, and spends the week on measure choices, failed jobs and live faults.
reach: The network architect reads the signed security measure version instead of asking for another summary.
System users see which restore is already signed and which failed backups are still open.
skills_to_grow: Write a security measure as fields a template can check before anyone changes a live system.
Separate a scheduled backup job from a recovery that still needs a signature.
State a fault fix and the part to replace before touching the live system.
role.ambitious_version: Every site runs from a signed security measure list, a named backup policy, and a fault queue that shows which fixes are still manual.
